mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW X5 30si engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full BMW X5 30si engine replacement typically costs £2,200-£4,200 supply-only for a rebuilt N52B30 unit, or £3,500-£5,500 fitted by a specialist. Used engines start from £800, while reconditioned units typically cost £1,600-£3,000. Prices vary by exact N52 variant (N52B30A / N52B30AF / N52B30BF). Professional fitting adds £800-£1,200 to any engine purchase. Rebuilt units include upgraded valvetronic and timing components. 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty on all rebuilt engines.

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the BMW X5 30si N52 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N52B30 family has three well-documented failure points: valvetronic motor failure (rough idle, reduced power), electric water pump failure (sudden overheating), and oil filter housing gasket leaks (burning oil smell). All three typically appear between 60,000-120,000 miles. Valvetronic motor replacement at specialist: £500-£900. Water pump replacement at specialist: £450-£750. Oil filter housing gasket at specialist: £300-£500. Catch issues early to avoid full engine replacement. N52 water pump failure can happen without warning - replace preventatively at 80,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW X5 30si reliable? How long does the N52 engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N52 is generally well-regarded for reliability - it's BMW's final naturally aspirated straight-six and is smoother and more characterful than the turbocharged engines that followed. With proper maintenance, N52 engines regularly exceed 150,000-200,000 miles. Annual oil changes (not BMW's extended intervals) are critical. Valvetronic motor and water pump are the main wear items. N52 engines are less problematic than N47/N57 diesel units. Many specialists report N52s reaching 200,000+ miles with preventative maintenance.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a high-mileage BMW X5 30si?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 2006-2008 X5 30si worth £2,850-£8,425, a £2,200-£4,200 rebuilt N52 engine can make financial sense if the body, gearbox, and interior are in good condition. The decision depends on the individual car's condition and your ownership horizon. Compare replacement cost against vehicle value (typically 40-70% on lower-value examples). If body and gearbox are sound, a rebuilt engine can add years of life. Used engine (£800-£1,600) is the budget option for short-term ownership. Rebuilt engine (£2,200-£4,200) offers warranty and peace of mind.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW X5 30si and the xDrive35i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 30si (2006-2008) uses the naturally aspirated N52B30 straight-six petrol engine producing 272hp. The xDrive35i (2009 onwards) replaced it with the turbocharged N55B30 producing 306hp - a significant power increase and different driving character. 30si: naturally aspirated, 272hp, smoother power delivery, simpler engine. 35i: turbocharged, 306hp, more torque, more complex (charge pipe, turbo issues). 30si is the choice for buyers seeking BMW's last naturally aspirated six. Engine codes are not interchangeable - always match the correct code.

mainEntity.name: Can I replace my BMW X5 30si engine with a different size or fuel type?

acceptedAnswer.text: Engine swaps to a different size or fuel type are technically complex and rarely cost-effective on the E70 X5. Stick to like-for-like replacement using the correct N52 engine code (N52B30A, N52B30AF, or N52B30BF) for your X5 30si. ECU, wiring loom, fuel system, and exhaust all differ between petrol and diesel. Transmission ratios differ between engine variants. Insurance must be notified of any non-standard engine swap. Specialist marketplace only recommends like-for-like code-matching for warranty coverage.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW X5 30si - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW X5 30si was introduced with the second-generation E70 X5 in 2006 as the entry-level petrol model, bridging the gap between the 3.0-litre naturally aspirated six-cylinder engine and the more powerful V8 options. It remained in production until the 2008 facelift, after which it was replaced by the turbocharged N55-powered xDrive35i.

commonProblems.h2: BMW X5 30si Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW X5 30si is powered exclusively by the N52B30 family - a 3.0-litre naturally aspirated straight-six petrol engine that represents BMW's final generation of naturally aspirated six-cylinder engines. While the N52 is generally well-regarded for its smooth power delivery and character, it has several well-documented failure points that become expensive as mileage climbs past 80,000-100,000 miles. Rebuilt N52 engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Valvetronic Motor Failure - Why the BMW X5 30si Loses Power and Idles Roughly
problems.rootCause: The N52's Valvetronic system uses an electric motor to adjust valve lift continuously. Over time, the motor's internal gears wear or the eccentric shaft sensor fails, triggering a failsafe mode that limits power and causes rough idling.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valvetronic motor and eccentric shaft sensor, recalibrate valvetronic system
repairOptions.longevity: 60,000-80,000 miles. Viable if caught before secondary damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valvetronic motor, VANOS solenoids, and timing chain tensioner
repairOptions.longevity: 80,000-100,000 miles. Recommended if multiple valvetronic/VANOS codes present.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt N52 engine with upgraded valvetronic components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: 100,000+ miles. Best option if valvetronic failure caused secondary damage or engine has other age-related issues.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2006-2008 BMW X5 30si in fair-to-good condition is valued at approximately £2,850-£8,425 in the UK market. With a rebuilt N52 engine costing £2,200-£4,200 supply-only (plus £800-£1,200 fitting), replacement cost represents 40-70% of vehicle value on lower-value examples. For an X5 30si worth under £5,000, a used or reconditioned engine may offer better value; for vehicles worth £6,000+, a rebuilt unit with warranty typically justifies the premium.
problems.recommendation: Valvetronic motor failure is rarely catastrophic if caught early - specialist replacement of the motor and sensor typically costs under £900 and restores full performance. However, if you're facing valvetronic failure on an X5 30si with over 100,000 miles and other age-related issues (oil leaks, cooling system wear), a full rebuilt engine with upgraded components may be the more cost-effective long-term solution. Always get a specialist diagnosis before committing.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N52B30 BMW X5 30si engine prices

problems.h4: Electric Water Pump Failure - Why the BMW X5 30si Overheats Without Warning
problems.rootCause: The N52 uses an electric water pump instead of a belt-driven mechanical pump. The pump's internal electronics and bearings fail over time, causing sudden coolant loss or complete pump failure - often without warning until the temperature gauge spikes.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace electric water pump, thermostat, and coolant
repairOptions.longevity: 60,000-80,000 miles. Recommended preventatively on N52 engines.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt N52 engine with new water pump and cooling system components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if overheating caused head gasket failure or block damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: See above. For a typical £2,850-£8,425 X5 30si, a preventative water pump replacement at a specialist (under £750) is excellent value and should be considered routine maintenance on any N52 approaching 80,000 miles.
problems.recommendation: The N52's electric water pump is a wear item - replace it preventatively at 80,000 miles or 10 years, whichever comes first. The cost of a failed pump that leads to overheating and head gasket failure is 5-10 times higher than preventative replacement. If your 30si has already overheated, have a compression test performed immediately - if the head gasket has failed, a full rebuild may be the only safe option.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for BMW X5 30si water pump replacement and N52 engines

problems.h4: Oil Filter Housing Gasket Leaks - Why the BMW X5 30si Loses Oil and Smells Burnt
problems.rootCause: The oil filter housing gasket degrades over time due to heat cycling, allowing oil to seep onto the exhaust manifold. This causes a burning oil smell and, if ignored, can lead to oil starvation and alternator damage from oil contamination.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Oil filter housing gasket replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil filter housing gasket, clean oil residue, top up oil
repairOptions.longevity: 80,000-120,000 miles. Viable if caught early - no secondary damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt N52 engine with new gaskets throughout, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil starvation caused bearing damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: See above. Specialist gasket replacement under £500 is cost-effective on any X5 30si worth more than £2,000.
problems.recommendation: The oil filter housing gasket leak is one of the most common N52 issues - and one of the cheapest to fix if caught early. Check for oil residue around the oil filter housing at every service. If you smell burning oil after a drive, have the gasket inspected immediately - the repair is under £500 at a specialist and prevents much more expensive engine damage.
